subject: FintechAI — pricing & latency trade-offs (token volumes + target $/1M tokens)
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + follow-up notes from today's discovery

Marissa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple clarifying questions: 

- Monthly active users: 2.5M, but only ~250k will hit the LLM flows per month initially.
- Typical prompt size: 150-450 tokens (median ~220).
- Expected average completions per user session: 3 responses.
- Target budget: goal is to keep inference spend under $3k–5k/month initially, with runway to scale to $20k/month if product proves out.

Questions: 
1) Do you have examples for unit economics expressed as $/1M tokens across your tiers (hosted vs dedicated)?
2) For our latency targets (p95 <= 700ms on median prompt length), would you recommend streaming or a dedicated low-latency tier?

Also attaching the spreadsheet we referenced with a few sample flows (I'll send separately if you need).

Thanks,
Alex
Product Lead — FintechAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechai.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fintechai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up notes from today's discovery

Alex — great to meet you. Appreciate the clear numbers — that helps a lot. High-level answers below and I've attached a short pricing sheet (pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) and a SE note on latency/cost trade-offs for your review.

Quick answers to your questions:
1) Unit economics: see the attached table, but top-line: hosted API (pay-as-you-go) starts at ~$7–12 per 1M tokens depending on model family and whether you enable streaming (streaming slightly higher due to connection overhead). Dedicated pools (reserved) can reduce to ~$2–5 per 1M tokens at high commit levels because of utilization gains + quantized variants.

2) Latency: for p95 <= 700ms on ~220 token prompts, our recommendations:
   - Start on our Dedicated Standard tier (if you can commit to a monthly reserved capacity) or Hosted Low-Latency tier for trial.
   - Streaming helps perceived latency for long outputs (users see tokens as they arrive) but has higher per-request overhead; batching reduces $/token but increases tail latency.

Next steps I suggest:
- I'll put together a brief mutual action plan (MAP) with pricing scenarios based on 250k MAU hitting LLM flows and your target budget ranges.
- Vivek (copied) can propose runtime/batching settings that meet your p95 target while keeping unit costs reasonable.

Sharing attachments: pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, latency_vs_cost_se_notes.pdf, and I'll follow up with a MAP doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up notes from today's discovery — SE notes on latency vs cost

Alex, Priya — quick technical notes to complement Marissa's pricing: 

Thanks for the prompt/volume breakdown. Two practical options to balance your p95 <= 700ms target with cost constraints: 

Option A — Low-latency hosted/dedicated instance (favor latency):
- Use a dedicated low-latency pool (pinned GPUs) or Hosted Low-Latency tier with minimal batching (batch size 1–2, max latency budget 150–200ms per token).
- Target: p95 ~500–700ms for 220-token prompts for the XL-class models.
- Cost: higher per-token (~$9–12 / 1M tokens on Hosted Low-Latency) because you pay for reserved capacity or pre-warmed instances.

Option B — Cost-optimized with async batching + streaming for perceived latency:
- Use standard dedicated pools with dynamic batching (batch windows 10–50ms), token-level streaming for user-perceived speed, and client-side prefetching.
- Target: p95 ~700–900ms (depends on burst patterns); median latency lower due to streaming.
- Cost: ~ $2–5 / 1M tokens on reserved at reasonable commit levels; pay-as-you-go will be higher.

Tuning knobs to use: batching window, max batch size, KV cache for repeated prefixes, response length cap, quantized model variants for lower cost.

SLO-driven pricing discussion:
- If you need contractual p95 SLAs we can discuss a priced SLA add-on. Typical structure: base unit price + SLA premium (e.g., +15–30% on unit price) for guaranteed p95 targets and routed capacity.

I'll attach a short SE note (latency_vs_cost_se_notes.pdf) with example numbers for your median token lengths and 250k active users.

If you want, we can run a 2-week proof-of-concept: we instrument tokens + latency and show projected $/1M tokens for your real traffic mix.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up notes from today's discovery — SE notes on latency vs cost

Thanks — super helpful. A couple follow-ups: 

- Our short-term budget is tighter (~$3k/month) while product-market fit is still unknown; long-term we can expand to $20k/month. Can you show a scenario that keeps us under $5k/month in the first 3 months (acceptable trade-offs on p95 up to 900ms)?
- We're very interested in a 2-week POC to get real numbers. What's needed from our side?
- For SLA pricing, can you provide a sample SLA premium/structure so we can budget?

If you can include a MAP with milestones (POC -> pilot -> commit) and an estimated cost curve (pay-as-you-go vs 3/6/12-month commit), that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechAI — pricing & latency trade-offs (token volumes + target $/1M tokens)

Alex / Priya — attached the Mutual Action Plan (mutual_action_plan_fintechai.docx) with a three-step engagement: 2-week POC (instrumentation + perf run), 6-week pilot (subset of users on Dedicated Standard), and scale commit (3/6/12 month pricing tiers). Highlights: 

- POC: we run your sample traffic (you provide replay CSV + example prompts), instrument tokens/latency. Estimated cost to Redwood: absorbed for sales-trial; we ask for a usage estimate so we can size the test.
- Pilot (if POC looks good): target cost under $5k/month via reserved micro-pool + streaming optimizations for perceived latency. We model scenarios in pricing_sheet_v2.pdf — sample: 250k users at 5% engagement (12.5k active sessions) – ~8–10M tokens/month; pay-as-you-go ~$80–120 / 1M tokens (estimate), reserved commit brings to ~$6–12 / 1M depending on model/quantization.
- SLA premium: for contractual p95 <=700ms add ~20% on top of the unit price and a minimal monthly commitment. Exact numbers depend on region and model family.

Action items: 
- Alex: share a 24–72 hour sample of replay traffic (CSV) and a short list of 10 representative prompts by EOD Monday.
- Priya: confirm legal/PO process and if you need a standard MSA or SOW.
- Vivek: run the sizing exercise and deliver a recommended config and expected p95/cost table by Monday.

I'll upload the MAP to the HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign for the POC SOW if you want to lock dates.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
